title: 2027 Subaru Forester Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: The 2027 Subaru Forester is a carryover model, and the only notable change is a slimmed-down lineup. Most prices remain unchanged from 2026.
body_markdown:
The Subaru Forester was completely redesigned for 2025, adding a hybrid model (covered separately) in addition to its non-turbo gas option. In 2026, a redesigned Wilderness model joined the lineup. Sitting in the very competitive compact SUV class, key rivals include the Toyota RAV4, the Honda CR-V, the Hyundai Tucson, the Nissan Rogue, and the Mazda CX-5. The 2027 Subaru Forester has four trims for the gas model: Base, Premium, Wilderness, and Limited.

## What’s New for the 2027 Subaru Forester


The Forester was completely redesigned in 2025, so this model is a carryover, and that includes most of the pricing. The minor changes that were made for 2027 include more standard equipment with the Limited trim level and the discontinuation of the Sport, Sport Onyx Edition, and Touring trims. It’s also worth noting that even though much of the vehicle pricing carries over from 2026, the destination fee increases from $1,450 to $1,525.


## Design


The Subaru Forester has always had an upright, blocky profile, and that didn’t change with the 2025 redesign. Standard wheels on this compact SUV are 17 inches, while the Limited trim upgrades to 18-inch wheels. All models come equipped with all-season tires except the Wilderness, which gets all-terrain tires. Speaking of the Wilderness, while there aren’t any appearance packages on the Forester, this off-road-focused trim has a different look and feel with chunky cladding, black wheels, bronze accents, and an exclusive Geyser Blue paint option.


## Powertrain


All Subaru Foresters come standard with all-wheel drive, and the only gas powertrain is a 180 horsepower 2.5-liter engine paired with a continuously variable transmission (CVT). While most trims get 8.7 inches of ground clearance, the off-road-focused Wilderness trim gets 9.3 inches along with better approach, departure, and breakover angles. Fuel economy for the Forester varies by trim. The EPA estimates between 24 mpg and 26 mpg in the city and between 28 mpg and 33 mpg on the highway, with the Wilderness trim getting the lowest numbers. Subaru also offers a Forester Hybrid (covered separately), which has more power and delivers 35 mpg in combined driving.


## Interior


The Subaru Forester is a five-passenger SUV, with rear legroom that sits in the middle of the pack for the compact SUV segment, besting both the Toyota RAV4 and Nissan Rogue. Maximum cargo space of 68.6 cubic feet behind the first row is very usable but not best-in-class. Available space behind the second row is 35.4 cubic feet. The interior of the base trim is bare bones, with cloth upholstery, a small infotainment screen, and manual seat adjustment. Synthetic leather or real leather seats are available on higher trim levels, as are power seat adjustments and a larger infotainment screen. A panoramic power moonroof and reclining rear seats become standard starting at the Premium trim, but aren’t available on the base.


## Technology


Even the base Subaru Forester gets Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, but it’s a wired connection and appears on a 7-inch screen (wireless versions are standard with other trim levels). The infotainment setup on the base is odd, with dual 7-inch screens stacked on top of each other so they fill the vertical space the more upscale 11.6-inch infotainment system needs. The top screen manages entertainment features, while the bottom screen manages vehicle functions such as HVAC controls. The base model also comes standard with a four-speaker audio system, one USB-A front charge port, a 12-volt power outlet on the front console, and a Wi-Fi hotspot (subscription required). Available tech features include navigation, a six-speaker audio system (Premium), an 11-speaker Harman Kardon audio system (Wilderness, Limited), front and rear USB-A and USB-C charge ports, and a 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster. With the discontinuation of the Touring trim, the Forester no longer has an available surround-view camera, but the Wilderness trim offers a 180-degree front-view camera for better trail visibility.

## Safety


The Forester gets Subaru's EyeSight safety suite that includes adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assist, lane-departure prevention, pre-collision braking, and a lead-vehicle start alert. Available safety features include blind-spot monitors, rear cross-traffic alert, automatic emergency steering, emergency lane-keep assist, and automatic reverse braking. The Forester received top marks from both the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). Although the IIHS hadn’t yet rated the 2027 model at the time of writing, the 2026 model was awarded the organization’s highest honors, with a Top Safety Pick+ award and Good ratings across the board. The NHTSA gave the 2027 model a five-star overall safety rating.


## Pricing and Release Date


The 2027 Subaru Forester is scheduled to go on sale in late 2026. At the time of writing, most pricing carried over from 2026, but as previously noted, destination fees have increased. The starting price for the base Forester is $31,520 (including destination fee), and the Premium trim starts at $33,520. The Limited starts at $39,120, with the Wilderness topping out at $41,020. The only package option available is on the Premium trim for $1,200, and includes a power rear liftgate, blind-spot monitors, and rear cross-traffic alert. Other than that, you have premium paint options that range from $395 to $890.
